episode.title: Resume sessions through the canonical persisted runtime-route resolver
episode.before: At parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the Desktop/TUI resume adapter independently read provider, base_url, and api_mode only from top-level model_config fields, then fell back to billing_provider. Gateway turns persist the latest effective route under model_config.gateway_runtime, while billing_provider can remain fixed to the first accounted provider. Consequently, a resumed session could combine its current stored model with a stale provider or endpoint and fail at the provider interface.
episode.after: At 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, Desktop/TUI resume obtains provider, base_url, and api_mode from the same SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime resolver used by CLI resume. That resolver prioritizes a valid nested gateway_runtime route, otherwise retains top-level route metadata and fills only a missing provider from a routable billing_provider. Resume therefore restores the latest persisted route without discarding legacy top-level endpoint metadata.
episode.diff: The change removes the TUI's hand-written provider-route extraction and delegates route resolution to the shared session-state reader. It adjusts the shared reader's fallback from an exclusive top-level-or-billing choice to a top-level route augmented with billing_provider only when provider is absent. Two regression tests cover nested runtime precedence over both a stale first-call billing provider and stale top-level route keys.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480 identifies parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe and describes the failure as Desktop resume ignoring model_config.gateway_runtime and pairing the current model with a first-call billing_provider.
Gateway turn synchronization records the effective provider, base_url, api_mode, and fallback state by replacing model_config.gateway_runtime and updating the stored model.
CLI stored_session_route already delegates persisted route interpretation to SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime before applying endpoint compatibility and per-model route derivation.

In the parent, _stored_session_runtime_overrides reads only top-level model_config provider/base_url/api_mode and falls back directly to billing_provider, so it cannot observe the newer nested gateway_runtime route.

The updated Desktop/TUI resume adapter calls SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row) and derives provider, base_url, and api_mode from its result while leaving service-tier and reasoning restoration in the consumer.

The shared reader continues to prefer a nested gateway_runtime containing a provider, but now augments surviving top-level base_url/api_mode fields with billing_provider via setdefault rather than returning billing_provider as a separate provider-only route.

test_resume_honors_gateway_runtime_over_first_call_billing_provider asserts that both Desktop and CLI resume select the nested openai-codex route and codex_responses mode instead of stale anthropic billing metadata.
test_resume_prefers_gateway_runtime_over_stale_top_level_keys asserts that Desktop resume chooses nested route fields over an older top-level provider, base URL, and API mode.
The commit records both added tests as red on the base with anthropic selected instead of openai-codex and green on the implementation head.
The implementation changes three files with 33 insertions and 24 deletions and passes git diff --check.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-persisted-runtime-route-by-freshness
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize heterogeneous persisted route representations by preferring the latest nested runtime snapshot, otherwise preserving legacy top-level endpoint fields and filling only a missing provider from a routable billing identity.

semantic_action.intent: Produce one coherent provider route from persisted session metadata without combining a current model with stale provider-interface metadata.
semantic_action.pre_state: Session metadata may contain a newer nested runtime snapshot, older top-level route fields, and a billing provider whose value reflects the first accounted call.
semantic_action.post_state: A nested route with a provider wins; otherwise top-level route fields survive and a routable billing provider supplies only an absent provider.
semantic_action.validation: Regression assertions verify nested runtime precedence over stale billing metadata and stale top-level route fields; the commit reports both assertions red on the parent and green on the implementation.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-resume-consumer-to-canonical-route-reader
candidate_atomics.description: Replace a resume surface's hand-written persisted-route interpretation with the shared resolver while retaining consumer-specific endpoint healing, reasoning, and service-tier behavior.

semantic_action.intent: Make independent resume interfaces restore the same persisted provider endpoint and protocol for a session.
semantic_action.pre_state: The resume adapter independently reads only top-level route fields and can disagree with another resume interface that already consumes the canonical nested-aware resolver.
semantic_action.post_state: The adapter consumes the canonical resolved route, so Desktop/TUI and CLI share route precedence while downstream consumer-specific normalization remains intact.
semantic_action.validation: Tests compare Desktop-derived route values with the CLI route and separately assert that Desktop honors the newest nested route over stale top-level data.

candidate_workflows.name: align-session-resume-with-the-latest-persisted-provider-route
candidate_workflows.description: Use when one interface persists a newer provider endpoint or wire protocol in a nested runtime snapshot but another resume interface reconstructs the route from older fields. Establish one precedence-aware resolver, then route the divergent consumer through it and validate cross-interface agreement.

workflow_graph.goal: Resume a stored session on the provider endpoint and protocol most recently used by that session across all supported resume interfaces.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Multiple persisted representations exist, their freshness differs, and at least one resume consumer independently interprets them, allowing stale provider metadata to be paired with the stored model.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All examined resume consumers obtain route fields from the same freshness-aware resolver, nested runtime state has explicit precedence, and legacy top-level endpoint metadata remains compatible with provider fallback.
unresolved_or_deferred: No cross-project resolution pattern is claimed from this single workflow.
GitHub issue body, review discussion, and status checks were unavailable in the supplied bundle.

The local environment lacked a directly runnable project pytest installation; executable validation is therefore represented by the checked-in regression assertions and the commit's recorded red-on-base/green-on-head result.

unresolved_questions: Whether CI ran broader session-resume coverage is unknown because status checks were unavailable.

The added tests directly cover nested-route precedence; preservation of top-level base_url/api_mode when provider is supplied only by billing_provider is established by implementation diff and commit rationale, but no newly added test isolates that legacy fallback combination.
